tasks.entryName: Prokhorov's theorem (tightness and relative compactness of probability measures on Polish spaces)
tasks.entryDescription: Compactness via finite partitions and diagonal subsequences; metric/weak-convergence tightness argument; transport through distribution functions in R.
tasks.routeTitle: Compactness via finite partitions and diagonal subsequences
tasks.currentSketch: Given tight (μ_n), choose compact K_j with μ_n(K_j)>1−2^{−j}; on each K_j, finite covers and a diagonal argument select a subsequence whose integrals converge on a countable convergence-determining family of bounded continuous functions. Tightness prevents mass escape, and the limiting positive functional is a probability measure, giving weak convergence.

existingReferences.label: Billingsley, Convergence of Probability Measures

tasks.routeTitle: Approximate by indicator rectangles/simple functions and monotone convergence
tasks.currentSketch: For nonnegative indicators of measurable rectangles the iterated integrals equal product measure. Extend to nonnegative simple functions by linearity, then arbitrary nonnegative measurable functions by monotone convergence (Tonelli); apply to positive/negative parts when ∫|f|<∞ to obtain Fubini.

tasks.entryDescription: Gaussian/approximate-identity regularization; inversion via contour or Fourier integrals; Plancherel plus density. State the hypotheses for each form.
tasks.currentSketch: First establish the identity for Schwartz functions by Fubini and Gaussian regularization (insert e^{−επ|ξ|²}, apply the Gaussian transform, then let ε↓0). Density of Schwartz functions in L² extends the isometry uniquely to a unitary Fourier transform; hypotheses differ for pointwise inversion versus L² Plancherel.

tasks.routeTitle: Plancherel plus density. State the hypotheses for each form
tasks.currentSketch: On Schwartz functions the Fourier transform is an L² isometry by the double-integral/Parseval identity, first justified with Gaussian damping and Fubini. Schwartz functions are dense in L², so the isometry extends uniquely to a unitary operator on L²; this proves the Plancherel formulation, while pointwise inversion needs additional hypotheses.

tasks.entryDescription: Variational/calculus of variations; Fourier-series proof for closed curves; Brunn–Minkowski and convex-geometric argument; symmetrization.
tasks.currentSketch: Parametrize a smooth simple closed curve by arclength with length L and enclosed area A. A maximizing curve exists after compactness/regularization; first variation of A−λL shows its curvature is constant, hence the optimizer is a circle. Its area is L²/(4π), giving A≤L²/(4π). The existence and regularity step is essential and is not supplied by the Euler–Lagrange calculation alone.

tasks.entryDescription: Variational/calculus of variations; Fourier-series proof for closed curves; Brunn–Minkowski and convex-geometric argument; symmetrization.
tasks.currentSketch: For a planar measurable set E, apply Brunn–Minkowski to E and a small disk εB: |E+εB|^{1/2}≥|E|^{1/2}+ε√π. For a sufficiently regular boundary, the outer parallel-area expansion is |E+εB|=|E|+ε·Per(E)+o(ε); compare first-order terms to obtain Per(E)≥2√(π|E|). Approximation extends the result to finite-perimeter sets.

tasks.entryDescription: Variational/calculus of variations; Fourier-series proof for closed curves; Brunn–Minkowski and convex-geometric argument; symmetrization.
tasks.currentSketch: Repeatedly Steiner-symmetrize a bounded region: each symmetrization preserves area and does not increase perimeter. A compactness argument gives a limit invariant under every direction of symmetrization, hence a disk; lower semicontinuity of perimeter shows the disk has no larger perimeter than the original region. This proves Per(E)≥2√(π|E|), with equality only for disks up to null sets.

tasks.entryDescription: Induction and slicing; transport-map/Jacobian argument; Prékopa–Leindler functional inequality.
tasks.currentSketch: For 1<p<∞, write ∫|f+g|^p≤∫(|f|+|g|)|f+g|^{p−1}; apply Hölder to each term and divide by ||f+g||_p^{p−1}. This yields ||f+g||_p≤||f||_p+||g||_p; endpoint p=1 is direct, p=∞ follows from sup. Assume measurable functions and finite norms.

tasks.entryName: Carathéodory's theorem for convex hulls in Rᵈ
tasks.entryDescription: Affine-dependence coefficient elimination; linear-programming basic feasible solutions; induction on support size.
tasks.currentSketch: If x=∑_{i=1}^mλ_i x_i is a convex combination with m>d+1, the augmented vectors (x_i,1) are linearly dependent: choose a nonzero relation ∑a_i x_i=0, ∑a_i=0. Vary λ_i→λ_i−t a_i until one coefficient hits zero while all remain nonnegative; repeat until at most d+1 remain.
